strengths: Addresses an important practical setting: unlearning using only the pretrained model and forgetting data. Contrasting target-class and irrelevant-class input sensitivities provides a concrete, testable algorithmic idea.
The evaluation includes three deletion settings, 15 baselines, multiple architectures, and results reported over five trials. This represents substantial experimental effort.

Several class-level results are strong: MU-Mis achieves an average accuracy gap of 0.07 on CIFAR-100 and 0.20 on CIFAR-20 Sea. On Tiny ImageNet with ResNet-18, it takes 83 seconds versus SalUn's 2630 seconds, with respective gaps of 0.15 and 0.06.

The sequential-unlearning experiments examine recovery of previously forgotten knowledge and include predictive KL divergence. The loss-component ablation also provides useful evidence that combining both sensitivity terms improves the forgetting–utility tradeoff.
weaknesses: The central theoretical connection is not established convincingly. Section III-B omits derivatives through the training trajectory and prediction probabilities without controlling the approximation error. The claim that the aggregate cross-sample residual in Eq. (5) is negligible does not follow from ReLU sparsity; correlated or nearly duplicated samples can violate it. Moreover, sensitivity to perturbing a training input is not equivalent to the effect of deleting that sample. The analysis therefore supports a heuristic motivation rather than the claimed withdrawal of sample contribution.

The privacy evaluation does not substantiate robust protection or indistinguishability from retraining. MIA reports the fraction of forgetting examples classified as members, without sufficient attack specifications or false-positive calibration. Lower values alone are inconclusive: on CIFAR-20 Sea, MU-Mis scores 1.25% versus retraining's 51.61%. Whole-dataset KL can also obscure discrepancies on the much smaller forgetting set. Stronger calibrated attacks, separate forgetting/retained-set comparisons, and a retrain-versus-retrain reference are needed.

The broad superiority claims exceed the results. In Table A5, random-subset deletion gives average gaps of 2.80 on CIFAR-10 and 2.36 on SVHN, versus 0.51 for finetuning and 0.47 for SalUn, respectively. CIFAR-10 test accuracy falls to 91.50%, versus 94.75% after retraining. The ViT speedup also carries a meaningful utility cost: Tiny ImageNet test accuracy is 82.17%, versus 85.92% for retraining. These limitations deserve prominent discussion.

The claimed ease of tuning and practical data-free deployment remain insufficiently demonstrated. Figure 9 studies stopping thresholds from 0.7 to 1.0, whereas reported configurations use values up to 3.0 and sequential experiments up to 10. Appendix C-D additionally introduces task-dependent reweighting with kappa=80, without isolating its contribution experimentally. The manuscript does not explain how these settings are selected without retained-data or retrained-model feedback.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the useful implementation appendix. No MU-Mis code release is identified, Table A7 omits configurations for random-subset experiments and ViT subclass deletion, and the variation captured by the five trials is insufficiently specified. Broader testing across deletion sizes, class selections, and independently pretrained models would help establish whether the reported advantages are reliable.
